items.informal_name: Equality of Determinants: Linear Map and Matrix Representation
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_5} [inst : CommRing A] {ι : Type u_7} [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι]
  (f : (ι → A) →ₗ[A] ι → A), (LinearMap.toMatrix' f).det = LinearMap.det f
items.informal_description: For a finite index set $\iota$ and a commutative ring $A$, the determinant of the matrix representation of a linear endomorphism $f : A^\iota \to A^\iota$ is equal to the determinant of the linear map itself. Specifically, if $[f]_B$ denotes the matrix of $f$ with respect to the standard basis $B$ of $A^\iota$, then $\det([f]_B) = \det(f)$.

items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $ A $, an $ A $-module $ M $, and a finite type $ \iota $ with decidable equality, this function constructs a ring homomorphism from the endomorphism ring $ \mathrm{End}_A(M) $ to $ A $ using a truncated basis of $ M $. The truncation ensures basis independence, making the determinant well-defined as a ring element.

items.informal_name: Alternating Map to Dual Evaluates as Determinant on Wedge Products
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $ R $, natural number $ n $, and $ R $-module $ M $, evaluating the alternating map $ \text{alternatingMapToDual} $ at the wedge product $ v_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge v_n $ (obtained via the canonical multilinear map $ \iota_{\text{Multi}} $) equals the determinant of the $ n \times n $ matrix whose $(i,j)$-entry is $ f_j(v_i) $, where $ f_j \in \text{Module.Dual}(R,M) $ and $ v_i \in M $.

The determinant of a linear map on a finite-dimensional module over a commutative ring is defined as the determinant of its matrix representation with respect to any basis, and this definition is independent of the choice of basis. This is achieved by lifting the determinant function through the matrix representation isomorphism, ensuring basis invariance via quotienting out basis choices with the truncated type.

items.informal_name: Determinant of Product of Linear Maps is Product of Determinants
items.informal_description: For a finite free module $ M $ over a commutative ring $ R $, and a family of linear endomorphisms $ f_i : M \to M $ indexed by $ \iota $, the determinant of the product map $ \prod_{i \in \iota} f_i \circ \text{proj}_i $ (where $ \text{proj}_i $ denotes projection to the $ i $-th component) is equal to the product of the determinants of each $ f_i $, i.e., $ \det\left(\prod_{i} f_i \circ \text{proj}_i\right) = \prod_{i} \det(f_i) $.

items.informal_name: Determinant of Linear Map Equals Determinant of Matrix Representation
items.informal_description: For any finite basis $ b $ of a module $ M $ over a commutative semiring $ A $ and any linear map $ f : M 	o M $, the determinant of $ f $ computed via the basis $ b $ is equal to the determinant of the matrix representation of $ f $ with respect to $ b $. Formally, $\det(f) = \det(\mathrm{toMatrix}_b(f))$.
